title: The 29th of September
subject: One picture, every reason to celebrate
blurb: Every one of these is a real thing somebody celebrates on the 29th of September - and some of them are birthdays. They are all in the picture. Name the missing word in each.

items.spot: A red heart with a hospital trace running across it.
items.hint: Five letters. Cardiovascular disease is the world's leading cause of death, and this day exists to say so.
items.note: Run by the World Heart Federation. Often confused with the 27th; it is the 29th.

items.template: International Day of Awareness of Food Loss and Food ___
items.spot: A bin with perfectly good food going into it - an orange, a wedge of cheese, bread.
items.hint: Five letters. Roughly a third of all the food the world grows never gets eaten.
items.note: Declared by the UN General Assembly in 2019.

items.template: ___mas, the feast of St Michael and All Angels
items.spot: An angel with spread wings holding a sword, a dragon under the point of it.
items.hint: Seven letters. The archangel who threw the dragon out of heaven, and the name the feast is built from.
items.note: One of the four English quarter days, when rents fell due and the harvest was in.

items.spot: A steaming mug, seen from the side.
items.hint: Six letters. The American one is today; the international one is two days later, on the 1st of October.
items.note: Which does mean you can reasonably celebrate it twice in a week.

items.template: Born today in 1547: Miguel de ___, who wrote Don Quixote
items.spot: A windmill, with a small lance pointed at it.
items.hint: Nine letters. Spain's greatest novelist, and the man who sent a knight to fight farm machinery.
items.note: The date is traditional rather than certain; he was baptised on the 9th of October.

items.template: Born today in 1571: ___, the painter of violent light and shadow
items.spot: A dark canvas with a face half lit, and a shaft of light falling across it.
items.hint: Ten letters. An Italian painter who killed a man over a tennis match and painted the best lighting in art history.
items.note: Born Michelangelo Merisi; known by the town he came from.

items.template: Born today in 1901: Enrico ___, Nobel laureate and builder of the first nuclear reactor
items.spot: An atom, a red nucleus with three electron orbits around it.
items.hint: Five letters. An Italian physicist. The question named after him asks where all the aliens are.
items.note: He built the first reactor under a Chicago squash court in 1942.

items.template: Born today in 1935: Jerry Lee ___, who played the piano standing up
items.spot: A piano keyboard with flames coming off the top of it.
items.hint: Five letters. They called him the Killer, and his signature song set a great ball of fire.
items.note: His career survived rather more scandal than most.

items.template: Born today in 1988: Kevin ___, one of the great scorers in basketball
items.spot: A basketball under a hoop and net.
items.hint: Six letters. Nicknamed the Slim Reaper, and about as hard to guard as the name suggests.

items.template: Born today in 1907: Gene ___, the singing cowboy
items.spot: A cowboy hat with a sheriff's star above it and a guitar neck below.
items.hint: Five letters. He sang about a red-nosed reindeer long before anyone animated it.
items.note: He is the only person with stars in all five Hollywood Walk of Fame categories.

items.spot: A badge shield with a star in the middle of it.
items.hint: Six letters. Australia remembers the officers who died in the line of duty.
items.note: Marked on the feast of St Michael, their patron saint - which is why it is today.

items.template: ___ Day, for the Chinese philosopher who taught the golden rule
items.spot: An open scroll or book under a tiled roof.
items.hint: Nine letters. Do not do to others what you would not want done to you - he got there first.
items.note: Taiwan keeps it as Teachers' Day.
